inputs.original_text: Water Not Coal is being sold as a grassroots campaign, but a signature drive is an easy way to channel public anger into a narrow request to the Government of Alberta while the real interests shaping the larger fight remain hidden. Corb Lund started it last month, and local canvassers are collecting signatures—but that doesn’t prove the campaign is independent or that decision-makers are on the public’s side. It looks more like a way to make people feel heard while keeping attention off who benefits from the outcome.
inputs.modified_text: Water Not Coal looks less like a genuine grassroots movement than a pressure valve: collect signatures, channel public anger into a narrow request to Alberta’s government, and give people the feeling they’ve been heard while the interests steering the larger fight stay out of view. Corb Lund started it last month, and local canvassers are gathering signatures, but that proves nothing about who’s really shaping the campaign—or who benefits from the outcome. The whole setup feels designed to keep scrutiny pointed in the safest direction.
